data.name: Help_Text
data.value:
Requirements Windows PC and PTZ camera with a compatible HTTP-CGI interface on a reachable network. The MSIX package includes .NET; other builds require the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime.
Supported commands matter, regardless of manufacturer or model: movement, zoom, stops and presets via /cgi-bin/ptzctrl.cgi?ptzcmd&… . IPv4 and HTTP on port 80 without authentication are required. Not every HTTP-CGI interface uses this command set.
Camera setup Under “Camera”, change and save the IP address. Cancel discards your changes.
Movement and presets Hold the arrow and zoom buttons; release to stop. Keyboard: arrow keys, numpad plus/minus and 1–6 or 9 for presets.
Each button recalls its assigned camera preset number. Keyboard shortcuts remain assigned to buttons. The app does not create camera positions automatically. Set up the desired position before recalling it for the first time.
Under “Buttons & presets”, choose names and camera preset numbers, then select “Save assignment”. Numbers: 0–89 or 100–254, if supported by the camera. Multiple users should agree on their number ranges. Duplicate numbers within a Windows account are blocked.
Aim the camera and select “Save position”. After confirmation, this overwrites the assigned camera preset. Check using “Recall position”. Names and assignments are stored locally per Windows account; positions are stored by the camera.
Automatic positions Under “Settings > Automatic positions”, choose a startup or exit position and select “Save automatic positions”. Without a selection, the camera will not move automatically. On exit, the exit position is recalled only after the stop has been confirmed. An HTTP response does not confirm that the camera has reached its target.
Demo mode Try the app without a camera under “Demo mode”. Left: stage and camera frame; right: simulated camera image, no live video. No network commands are sent. Demo names, assignments, positions and automatic positions apply to this session only; your camera settings are preserved.
Language Under “Language / Sprache”, choose the Windows setting, Deutsch, English or Español and save. The language will be applied the next time you start the app. Unsupported Windows languages use English.
Connection problems Check the IP address, network and power supply. HTTP errors may indicate an incompatible camera interface.
When switching windows or opening settings, the app attempts to stop the camera. If a stop is not confirmed, the camera may continue moving: check the camera and use its own controls if needed.
